name: Random bar wipe

source.description: 3 inspected reference films (batch-3, batch-6, 2026-11-26): a pencil-on-paper launch film leaves its dark payoff section through horizontal bars of random length.

technique: Horizontal bars of random length and position appear across the frame, merge into full cover and clear to reveal the next scene. It reads as a quick digital redraw, faster and less formal than a straight wipe.
purpose: A quick, informal change of register between sections, read as a digital redraw.
visual_behaviour: Horizontal bars of random length and position grow across the frame until it is covered, then clear in the same pattern onto the next scene, in about 0.3 s.
mechanics: 10-14 horizontal bars of 1/16-1/10 of the frame height with seeded x offsets and lengths; bars in the incoming scene's colour grow in from random x over about 0.12 s until full cover at about 0.15 s; the scene swaps under cover; bars clear in the same pattern over 0.15 s (ref-2860712d4e 11.21-11.51 s, 0.3 s in all, 30 fps sheet).

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: PRNG seed for the bar pattern

use_cases: Leaving a dark section for a light canvas
A quick change of register between sections
failure_modes: An unseeded pattern changes between renders
Too slow reads as a broken screen

implementation.approach: 10-14 bars of 1/16-1/10 of the frame height in an overlay layer, with seeded x offsets and lengths, grow in the incoming scene's colour over about 0.12 s to full cover at 0.15 s; swap the scene under cover; clear in the same pattern over 0.15 s. Seed the pattern with the Studio PRNG. Not built (the overlay works like the curtain type of Studio.transition).

provenance.observed: Horizontal bars of random lengths cover a dark chalkboard scene and uncover the paper canvas in 0.3 s.
Stepped variant: orange bars of different heights rise from the bottom and cover the frame (12.79-12.99 s) onto the end card.
Pixel-block variant (check 0.37): square blocks dissolve from the top-right corner across the frame while a black ball rolls in (3.33-3.60 s).

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown).
